text: Low ceiling, stained ferrocrete walls, a bar made from a freighter cargo door welded to drum supports. Smell of fryer oil and ship hydraulics. The bartender wipes a glass with a rag that used to be a shirt.

The booths are cut from old escape pod hulls, bolted to the floor. Tube lights buzz in two of the three sockets. A spacer at the counter slides a credit chit across without looking up; the bartender slides a bottle back the same way.

Sheet metal walls, a ceiling fan turning lopsided overhead. The air tastes faintly of ozone from the docking bay one wall over. A serving droid with a cracked photoreceptor delivers drinks and never spills.

A long narrow room, no windows, the door propped open with a fuel drum. Engine wash from outside ruffles the napkins every few minutes. A Sullustan at the end of the bar laughs at nothing twice and goes quiet.

The place is lit in red and amber. Booths along one wall, a sabacc table dark in the corner. A serving girl threads through the room with four mugs balanced on a forearm, calling drink orders over her shoulder in three languages.

A wall-mounted holo plays podracing footage on a loop with the sound off. The bar smells of stale ale and someone's reheated nerf-meat. A Rodian dozes upright in the corner booth, drink half-finished in his hand.

The bar is shaped like a horseshoe, scarred with carved initials and burn marks. Pipes overhead drip condensation into a metal pan with a soft tonk every few seconds. The bartender refills a cup before the spacer thinks to ask.

Plastoid stools, mismatched tables, a sign behind the bar reading 'NO BLASTERS DRAWN' in six languages. The smell of charged ozone says the place has its own dampeners. A spacer drops his hand back to the table after his friend nudges him.

Concrete floor, a drain in the middle of it. Light comes from caged bulbs and a flickering neon sign that buzzes in Huttese. A patron at the corner table eats stew one-handed; the other hand stays under the table.
The walls vibrate faintly with every launch from Pad Nine. Drinks come in dented metal cups. A Twi'lek bartender pulls a bottle from a shelf marked with hand-scrawled tape: 'HOUSE,' 'GOOD,' 'DON'T.'

A pair of overhead fans push hot air around. The wall behind the bar is plastered with old bounty notices, layers deep, some scratched out. The bartender peels a fresh one off a pad and presses it flat over an older face.

Long shotgun room, a door at each end, the back one chained shut with a padlock. The smell of fuel sits in the corners. Two spacers at the bar fall silent every time the front door opens, then resume.

The booths are upholstered in cracked vinyl patched with engine tape. A spacer at the bar argues prices with the bartender, neither raising their voice. The serving droid rolls past with a tray and squeaks at the third wheel.

Bare bulbs strung on cables, half of them out. A keg taps somewhere off-camera with a thump. A pilot at the corner table eats a fried nerf-loaf with his fingers and reads a flimsi spread out flat across the wood.

The bar smells of caf gone bitter and stim-sweat. A blast door behind the counter is propped half-open with a bottle. The bartender ducks back there for a minute and comes out wiping her hands on her apron.
Low-ceilinged, packed wall to wall. Conversation pitched just under the music. A spacer flags down the bartender by tapping his empty cup three times against the bar and waits without looking up.

Half the lights are red emergency strips, the other half are blue work lamps salvaged from somewhere. The bar smells of solvent. A patron at the counter is wiping engine grease off his hands with a bar napkin.
A live band of three Bith plays in a corner, dust on their instrument cases. Music sits low under the talk. A serving girl spins past with empties stacked five high on a tray, never breaking step.

The whole place tilts about three degrees — the building was bolted onto repurposed landing struts and never quite settled. Drinks slide if you don't pin them. A pilot at the bar steadies his glass without looking, mid-sentence.
Stale air, recycler buzzing somewhere overhead, the smell of fried tubers from the back. A patron at the counter stares into his cup like it owes him money and hasn't spoken in twenty minutes.

The door slides open and three Imperial naval ratings in working coveralls duck in. Conversation drops half a notch and stays there. The bartender doesn't change anything about how she's polishing the glass.

Smells of recycled atmosphere and burnt coolant. A holo screen behind the bar shows departure schedules with half the entries blinking RED. The bartender slaps the side of the unit; one entry flips back to green.

The music cuts. Every head in the room comes up at once. Somewhere outside, a heavy door is being kicked. The bartender ducks below the counter and comes back up with a slug-thrower laid across the bartop.
Floor sticky in patches, ceiling fans turning, a holo of some podrace playing silent above the door. A spacer at the bar laughs once, sharp, then puts his head down on the wood and doesn't move.
Old bench seating cut from passenger liner salvage. The cushions are split, foam coming through. A serving boy maybe twelve years old works the tables, ducking under elbows with a tray of empties.

Walls hung with souvenir flags, racing pennants, a stuffed mynock. The smell of cheap spice burns at the edge of the air. A patron at the bar pays in offworld coin and the bartender weighs each piece on a small scale.

Outside, a freighter lifts off and the windows rattle for a full minute. Inside, no one looks up. The bartender pours through it without spilling, eyes on the cup, finishing the pour as the last vibration dies.

Two patrons at separate booths are watching the same booth — the empty one nearest the back door. Neither of them has ordered. The bartender wipes the bar three times in front of where the players are standing.

Half the bottles behind the bar have hand-lettered labels. The other half are dusty and untouched. A spacer asks for a specific brand and the bartender pulls one of the dusty bottles down without comment.
The chairs are bolted to the floor — old policy from rougher days. A small bandstand stands empty. A spacer in the front booth keeps glancing at the door, then catching himself, then doing it again.
A row of helmets hangs above the bar — pilot helmets, mining helmets, one stormtrooper helmet with a crack down the visor. The bartender pours under it without ever looking up at it.

The lights flicker, hold steady, flicker again. No one comments. The serving droid pauses mid-roll each time, then resumes. A patron at the bar refills his own glass from a bottle the bartender left in front of him.

A blast door slams shut at the far end of the room and the bouncer locks it from outside. The bartender doesn't pause her pour. A spacer at the counter says, 'Curfew already?' and somebody laughs without humor.
A counter for ordering, a wall for drinking, no seats at all. Patrons stand shoulder to shoulder against the wall, drinks in hand. A pilot finishes hers, sets the cup on the floor, and walks out.
The whole back wall is one window onto the docking bays. A freighter is being unloaded under hot work lights. A patron at the bar watches it crate by crate, mouthing numbers.

Two booths have been pushed together at the back. Whatever was on them has been swept onto the floor — broken glass, a spilled drink. No one is sitting there. The bartender does not look toward the back.

A serving droid in mismatched plating — chest from one model, head from another — works the room. It pauses at each table to recite the day's specials in three languages, ending each list with the same phrase: 'No credit.'
The floor slopes toward a drain in the center. A bucket of soapy water sits by the door, sponge floating in it. A spacer steps around the bucket without looking and slides onto a stool.

Old Republic-era light fixtures, half of them dead. The bar itself is newer — repurposed durasteel, recently welded. A bartender wipes condensation off a fresh-poured mug and slides it to a patron whose name she doesn't ask.

The place smells of fried mealworm and engine coolant in roughly equal measure. A serving girl carries a tray with one hand and balances a bottle on her head with the other, calling for the players' table.

Every privacy field in the bar drops at once. A spacer at the booth nearest the door is already standing, jacket half-on. The bartender slides a duffel across the counter to no one visible and goes back to wiping glasses.
A heavyset Weequay at the corner booth. He's the only one whose hands are above the table. Anytime someone new walks in, he counts them under his breath and starts over.
A Devaronian bartender with one ear notched. Listens to every order twice, then repeats it back in a different language, and the patron always nods.
An old human pilot at the bar, fingers stained with hyperdrive carbon. Calls every freighter 'she' and corrects himself out loud each time, then immediately does it again.
A Twi'lek dock supervisor in a grease-streaked tabard. Knows everyone's name in the room and uses none of them — calls every patron 'captain' regardless.
A Rodian with a chronograph on each wrist showing different times. Glances at one, then the other, then one again, three times a minute.
A young human woman in a flight jacket two sizes too big, sleeves rolled. Listens hard whenever anyone mentions ship parts, then pretends she wasn't.
A Trandoshan with a long scar across his snout, sitting alone with three empty glasses already lined up. Doesn't drink from the fourth — he counts it, then orders another.
A wiry human in coveralls with no station patch — the place where one used to be is faded but unmistakable. Sits with his back to the wall and faces the door.
A Bothan with grey through her fur, datapad face-down on the table. Asks every server who passes the same question — 'What time is it?' — and writes the answer down each time.
A Quarren bartender with one tentacle that twitches whenever a credit chit changes hands at any table. Doesn't otherwise react.
A spice-thin human in stained civilian black, soldier's spine and grey at the temples. Will not say the word 'Empire' — calls them 'the current lot' and changes the subject.
An Ithorian in a stevedore's harness, both hands wrapped in old burn-tape. Speaks only to ask 'Where are you going next?' to anyone who orders a drink alone.
A Kel Dor in a worn flight mask, one cracked lens patched with sealant. Refers to the players in the third person even when addressing them directly.
A human in a half-buttoned Imperial naval rating's tunic, no insignia, no rank tabs. The boots are still regulation. Pretends not to hear questions about his ship.
A Mirialan freighter captain in faded coveralls, geometric tattoos along her jaw. Repeats the last word of every sentence in a whisper, then denies it.
A wiry Aqualish at the bar, one tusk capped in dull metal. Switches languages every time the door opens and goes back to the previous one once it shuts.
A small Chadra-Fan perched on a stool, feet not quite reaching the floor. Names every drink she sees — even ones at other tables — in a continuous, quiet running commentary.
A burly human, beard salted with grey, missing the smallest finger of his left hand. Buys a round for any group he overhears speaking Mando'a and then sits back down.
A Sullustan freighter pilot with goggles pushed up onto her forehead, leaving rings of clean skin around the eyes. Talks to her drink, not her companions, and asks it questions she answers herself.
A Nautolan dockworker with a fresh stitched cut across one head-tress. Cuts every conversation off after exactly three exchanges and walks to a different stool.
An older Zabrak woman, horns capped in tarnished silver, sleeves rolled past faded gang ink. Asks the players' names, then asks again ten minutes later, then asks one more time, friendly each time.
A protocol droid with a missing arm and one mismatched leg, polishing the same spot on the bar. Greets every entering patron in flawless Coruscanti, then in flawless Huttese, then in flawless Bocce.
A wizened Toydarian fluttering above his stool because the seat is broken. Settles disagreements between strangers without being asked, declaring 'fair, fair' until both parties shut up.
A young Mandalorian in patchwork beskar — three different clan colors painted over each other. Won't accept a drink from anyone but pays for everyone at the bar in the round he just left.
A heavyset human in a midnight-blue jacket has paid the bill three times in the last hour. Each time, a different person at the bar gets the drink.
A Twi'lek in spacer leathers slides a credit chit across the bar without speaking. The bartender slides back a small key — not a credit chit. The Twi'lek pockets it and walks out the back.
A Rodian deckhand is loudly retelling the same story for the third time, louder each round. Several patrons at her table have stopped responding but kept their drinks.
A grizzled human pilot at the bar is field-stripping a hold-out blaster on a bar napkin. The bartender places his refill carefully on the dry side of the wood and walks away.
A Bith bartender writes something on the back of a coaster and slides it under a patron's empty glass. The patron pockets the coaster, leaves the glass, walks out without paying.
A Sullustan in oil-streaked coveralls is showing off a wrist-comm to the patron next to her. 'Three jumps,' she keeps repeating. 'Three jumps in twelve hours. Watch.'
A wiry Trandoshan is counting credits onto the bar one chit at a time, slowly. He's at fourteen. The bartender stands across from him, arms folded, not pouring.
A Devaronian in a stained dockmaster's tabard is arguing with the bartender, voice low. 'It's not for me. I told you it's not for me.' He keeps wiping his palms on his thighs.

An older Mirialan in faded captain's stripes is being escorted to the door by the bouncer. She isn't resisting. As she passes the players, she says clearly: 'Don't take the Kessel run job. It's the same one.'
A spacer in a flight jacket two sizes too small is doing pull-ups on the doorframe for a small audience and a wager. He drops down at twelve, takes a drink, and starts over.
A Weequay in mining gear is selling something from inside his vest to a nervous human at the corner table. Whatever it is, it changes hands wrapped in oilcloth, no eye contact.
A young human in a flight crew jacket is loudly looking for crew. 'Coreward run, four nights, splits even.' Nobody at the bar is looking up. He keeps repeating it.
A Quarren bartender is refusing to take a patron's credits — pushing the stack back across the bar twice now. She isn't speaking. The patron's voice is rising; hers stays silent.
A Zabrak with a fresh swollen eye is asking, table by table, if anyone saw 'a tall human in a green coat' come through. Most shake their heads. None of them look him in the face.
A Pantoran in mismatched flightsuit pieces is signing for a delivery droid at the door — datachip handed over, food crate hauled in. The crate is too heavy to be food. She tips well.

An old human in a faded merchant marine coat is buying his own table a third round and is the only one still drinking. He keeps gesturing at the empty chair beside him and saying, 'When she gets here.'
A heavyset Twi'lek bouncer is removing a patron — by the collar, not the arm — through the front door. The patron is laughing. The bouncer isn't. Neither says anything.
A Bothan in a half-cape sets a datapad face-down on the bar and orders a drink she doesn't touch. She nudges the datapad two centimeters to the left, then back, then left again.
A Sullustan in a deck crew vest is photographing the bar's bottle shelf with a cheap holocam, pretending to be drunk. He's not drunk. He's getting every label.
A Kel Dor in a worn breath mask is rolling dice on the bartop, betting against herself. She wins three in a row, mutters 'cheating,' sweeps the dice up, restarts.
A wiry human in stained mechanic's coveralls is arm-wrestling a Wookiee. She's losing. She's also laughing. She buys the next round before the wrestle is decided.
A grey-furred Bothan is paying for the players' table without making it obvious — slipping credits to the serving girl as she passes, eyes never leaving his own drink.
An Aqualish in a heavy work harness is ordering for a person who isn't there — describing them to the bartender by smell, not appearance. The bartender pours the drink anyway.
A human in dock crew coveralls keeps walking out the front door, then back in, then out again, every few minutes. Each return, he orders the same drink. The bartender lines them up untouched.
A scrawny Sullustan dockhand asleep with his head on his arms in the second booth.
An older human in stained coveralls nurses a mug of something steaming, gloves off, hands red and chapped.
A Rodian in deck crew greys, drink half-finished, scrolling a datapad slowly.
A Twi'lek server in a stained apron leans against the back of the bar, taking a moment off her feet.
A Devaronian deckhand at the counter, paying his tab from a battered pouch coin by coin.
An Ithorian dockmaster at the third booth, eating a bowl of mush slowly, methodically.
A young Mirialan freighter crew member, head down on a datapad, ignoring the room.
An old human pilot at the bar, white-haired and quiet, sipping from a tall thin glass.
A Bith musician on break at a side stool, instrument case at her feet, drink untouched.
A Quarren shipping clerk in a stained vest at a corner table, ticking through a flimsi list with a stylus.
A scrawny human kid, maybe fourteen, leaning against the doorway with a delivery satchel.
A Zabrak in faded leathers, horns scuffed and chipped, drinking alone at the end of the bar.
A Nautolan in a heavy weatherproof coat at a window booth, head-tresses dripping faintly onto the table.
A Chadra-Fan curled on a wide stool, tail wrapped around its feet, picking at a plate of fried something.
A Pantoran in pilot's blue, blue tattoos faded on the cheeks, drinking water from a tin cup.
An Aqualish dockhand asleep upright, drink balanced precariously in one tusked hand.
A Toydarian hovering near the ceiling fan to cool off, drink in one tiny hand.
An old Weequay in a stevedore's tabard at a side table, eyes closed, a half-finished plate in front of him.
A young Kel Dor on his first leave, breath mask gleaming new, flipping a credit chit absent-mindedly.
A Trandoshan freight handler with a bandaged forearm, working through a bowl of stew with a wooden spoon.
A Bothan dockworker is paying her tab and shrugging into a heavy jacket.
A serving droid is wiping down a recently vacated table, stacking empties in the crook of one arm.
A young human in a freighter crew jacket is ordering a round and counting heads on her fingers.
A Sullustan deckhand is asking the bartender something across the counter, gestures small.
An old Twi'lek pilot is paying her bill, leaving a few coins on the bartop for the server.
A Devaronian freight handler is unloading a small crate at the back door for the bartender.
An Ithorian dockworker is reading a flimsi printout, frowning, eating absent-mindedly.
A Rodian crew member is on the comm, voice low, finger in the other ear to block the bar noise.
A young Quarren server is wiping down the bar in long, practiced strokes between orders.
A Mirialan pilot is filling a thermos at the bar, the bartender pouring caf into the wide top.
A Nautolan freighter crew member is signing for a small delivery from a porter droid at the door.
An old human merchant is dozing off mid-sentence into his own drink, jerking awake every few seconds.
A Zabrak dockhand is laughing — not at anything in particular — at a holo show playing soundless above the bar.
A Chadra-Fan freight runner is climbing onto a stool, struggling, settling, immediately gesturing the bartender over.
A Toydarian bookmaker is taking small wagers from a small cluster of patrons, scribbling notes on a flimsi pad.
A Pantoran in deck crew blue is feeding small scraps of jerky to a small lizard perched on her shoulder.
An Aqualish in heavy gloves is removing them one finger at a time before picking up a drink.
A Weequay deckhand is paying for the round behind him without turning around — credits over his shoulder.
A Trandoshan freight loader is flexing a sore claw, working it through a slow circle, then signaling for another drink.
A scrawny Bith bartender, off shift, is loading sheet music into an instrument case on the floor by his stool.
A human in pilot's blacks is sliding a flask into an inside pocket and finishing the bar's drink to cover for it.
An old Devaronian is feeding pieces of dried meat to a small ratlike creature in his coat pocket.
A Rodian in dock crew greys is methodically writing names on the back of a coaster and crossing them out.
A Twi'lek in a stained tabard is hauling a fresh keg up from a hatch behind the bar.
An old human spacer is rolling a flimsi smoke between his fingers but not lighting it — house policy taped behind the bar.
A young Sullustan is sweeping broken glass from beneath a stool into a battered dustpan.
A Quarren freight handler is finishing a drink in one long pull, paying, and walking out without speaking.

A Kaminoan in immaculate offworld silks at the corner table, drinking distilled water with a slice of fruit. Studies every entering patron for exactly two seconds and then dismisses them with a small head turn.
A masked Mandalorian in full beskar at the bar, helmet on, drinking through a slot mechanism with deliberate small sips. Hasn't moved her feet in twenty minutes.
A Hutt minor in a hoverpalanquin is being eased through the front door by two heavyset guards, dictating drink orders to one of them in a soft growl. The bartender is already pouring.

A duelling-scarred human at the end of the bar, dressed for the opera. Holds her wine glass by the stem with three fingers, the other two extended perfectly straight, and never lets the stem touch the bar.
Two Trandoshans at the corner table, identical posture, identical drinks. When one tastes, the other waits a half-beat, then tastes. Same pattern, every sip.
A human freighter captain and her Wookiee co-pilot at the second booth. She tells stories; he corrects details with a single short growl, and she always laughs and amends without arguing.
Two human women in identical battered flight jackets — same patches, different shoulders. Whenever one drinks, the other watches the door. They rotate every few minutes without speaking.
A Rodian and a Devaronian, both old, both bald, both quiet. They share a chessboard between their drinks. The Rodian moves; an hour later the Devaronian moves; neither speaks.
A Twi'lek mother and her teenage child at a side booth, both in deckhand coveralls. The mother is teaching; she points to other patrons and the child quietly names which ship they came in on.
An Aqualish and an Ithorian sit shoulder to shoulder at the bar, neither speaking. They finish each other's drinks — the Aqualish takes the Ithorian's, the Ithorian takes the next one. Switched once.

Two Bothans, one grey-furred, one young, in a back booth. The young one talks; the grey one listens and writes nothing, but corrects the young one with a single small headshake whenever a detail is wrong.
A Mirialan and a Sullustan are passing a single datachip back and forth across their table — each time, one slides it, the other examines, slides it back. Eight times so far.
Two human pilots in matching merchant marine jackets are arm-wrestling for the bar tab. They keep stopping mid-grip to drink. No one's winning. The bartender keeps adding to the total.
A Zabrak and a Nautolan at a back table are arguing in whispers — heads close together, eyes on the door, glasses untouched. The Zabrak keeps shaking his head; the Nautolan keeps nodding.

Two stormtroopers in armor, helmets on the bar beside their drinks, are halfway through a meal. They eat with the precision of soldiers and laugh at almost nothing. The bartender pours them carefully measured drinks.
Two human freighter crew at a side table, halfway through a meal, talking shop.
A Sullustan and a Rodian at the bar, drinks half-finished, swapping news in low voices.
Two old Devaronian dockhands at a side booth, sharing a plate of fried tubers, no conversation.
A Twi'lek and an Aqualish at the third booth, leaning on each other tired, almost asleep over empty plates.
Two young human deckhands at a high table near the door, laughing at something on a shared datapad.
A Mirialan and a Quarren at the bar, drinks identical, talking about nothing at moderate volume.
Two Trandoshan freight handlers at a corner booth, working through a pile of identical sausages.
An old human pilot and his protocol droid at a corner table, droid not drinking, the pilot quietly explaining a starchart.
Two Zabrak dockworkers at the second booth, eating with their hands, no plates.
A Pantoran and a Bith at a side booth, the Bith reading sheet music, the Pantoran sketching the Bith.
Two Weequay in stevedore tabards at the bar, drinking quietly, taking turns paying.
Two human dockhands are sharing a plate of fried mushrooms and bickering, mouths full, about a shipping schedule.
A Twi'lek bartender and a Sullustan supplier are tallying invoices at the end of the bar, fingers moving over a flimsi.
Two old Ithorian dockworkers are shuffling toward the door, drinks finished, helping each other into heavy coats.
A Rodian and a young human are settling their tab with the bartender, the human counting change twice.
Two Quarren freight handlers are toasting something — small, private — and drinking together in a single pull.
A Mirialan and an Aqualish are working through a shared plate of stew and trading bits of bread back and forth.
Two scrawny human deckhands are pooling credits on the bar, counting twice, then ordering one drink between them.
A Bith musician and a Pantoran patron are settling at the back booth, the musician unpacking a small kloo horn from a case.
Two Trandoshan freight handlers are paying their tab in offworld currency, the bartender weighing each coin in turn.
An old human spacer and a young Zabrak are settling into the back booth with two plates and one bottle between them.

Four spacers at the round table near the door — different species, identical posture, all facing outward. Whenever someone enters, every one of them clocks the newcomer in the same half-second and then resumes drinking.
A crew of six in matching merchant-marine jackets, sleeves cut at the elbow. They drink, talk, laugh — but when a server passes their table, the whole crew goes still in unison until she's past.
Three Mandalorians in mismatched beskar are settling into the back booth one at a time, weapons placed openly on the table in a row. The bartender brings the bottle without being asked.
A round table of five freighter crew — three humans, a Sullustan, a Rodian — halfway through a long meal, food everywhere.
A booth of four Twi'lek dockworkers, drinks lined up, conversation low and constant.
Three Imperial naval ratings in working coveralls at the front table, helmets on the bench beside them, drinking quietly.
A long table of seven dockhands — Devaronian, Quarren, Aqualish, the rest human — passing a single bottle around in turn.
A booth of four Bith musicians on break, instrument cases stacked beside them, sharing a single plate of food.
Three old human pilots at the central round table, white hair, identical drinks, no conversation.
A noisy table of five young deckhands — mixed species — sharing two plates of food and three drinks.
A group of four Sullustans is settling their tab and shrugging into matching freighter crew jackets.
A round table of six is toasting something — birthdays, contracts, something — drinks raised, voices loud, then drinking.
A scrawny human kid in a delivery satchel sidles up to the players' table and asks, quietly, if they're the ones who answered the comm posting. He doesn't say what posting.
The bartender slides a drink the players didn't order across the bar and says, 'Compliments of the booth at the back.' The booth at the back is empty.
A Bothan at the bar catches one of the players' eyes, taps a credit chit on the bartop twice, and tilts her head toward the back door.
An older Twi'lek freighter captain at the next stool mentions one of the players by ship name to her companion, then changes the subject without looking over.
A serving droid delivers a flimsi with the players' drinks. On it is a docking bay number and a time forty minutes out. No signature.
A Rodian in deck crew greys walks past the players' booth and drops a small wrapped package onto the seat between them without breaking stride.
Someone is loudly looking for a pilot at the bar — coreward run, paying double — and keeps describing the route in ways that match a job the players turned down on the last world.
The bartender, wiping down the bar in front of the players, says quietly, 'The man two booths over asked who you came in with. I told him I don't know your faces.'
The local newscast on the wall holo loops to a missing-persons bulletin. The face on screen is sitting at the bar, four stools from the players.
A Sullustan deckhand drops onto the stool next to one of the players and asks, friendly, where they're shipping out to. She listens too carefully to the answer.
A serving girl leans in to clear the players' table and says, low, 'My uncle says the docking bay you're parked in flooded an hour ago. Thought you should know.' She doesn't say who her uncle is.
An old Devaronian at the next table raises his glass slightly toward the players and says, 'Long time since I saw that patch on a jacket. Long time.' Then he goes back to his drink.
A street kid runs in, scans the room, runs out. A minute later the door slides open for two heavyset humans in matching jackets who linger inside the doorway scanning faces.
The bartender comes over with a refill the players didn't order and says, 'Three of you should leave through the kitchen. The fourth stays at this booth. Decide quick.'
Two Trandoshans at the corner booth have stopped pretending not to watch the players. One has been on the comm for two minutes. The other has emptied his hands.
A man in dock crew coveralls slides into the booth across from the players and says, 'I think you've got my drink.' His coveralls have someone else's name patch.
An Imperial naval rating in working coveralls comes over and asks, polite, if the players have seen the man whose face is on his datapad. The face matches one of the players.

A heavyset Aqualish bouncer comes up to the players' booth and says, quietly, that the owner would like to know who's covering the tab, because the man who left it was very specific about the players paying.
A Twi'lek at the next stool spills her drink on one of the players, apologizing loudly, and palms a folded flimsi into the player's pocket while doing it.
A serving droid rolls up and recites, in the players' direction: 'Customer in Booth Seven advises that the back exit is no longer recommended.' It rolls away before any of them can ask.
A wiry Zabrak with a fresh swollen eye sits at the bar where one of the players can see him and starts loudly telling the bartender about 'the offworlders who ran out on Vrek's job.'

A small protocol droid in mismatched plating wheels up to the players' booth and announces, 'I have a delivery for the captain. Which of you is the captain?' Several patrons at nearby tables look over.
An old human pilot at the bar gets up, weaves over to the players' booth, and asks if they remember him. They don't. He keeps standing there.
The front door is locked from the outside — a heavy thunk audible across the room. The bartender swears once, softly, and disappears into the back.
Three stormtroopers in armor have just entered the bar. The lead one is consulting a datapad, looking up at the room, looking back at the datapad. He's beginning to look at the players' booth.
A heavyset Weequay in mining gear has crossed the bar and is now standing at the end of the players' booth. He has not spoken. His hand is on the hilt of a vibroknife on his belt.
Outside the windows, blue light strobes — port authority enforcement. Patrons at the front are already moving toward the back. The bartender is locking the till.
A Mandalorian in scarred beskar enters the bar, helmet on, and stops just inside the door. The room quiets in waves. The bartender places a bottle and a single glass at the empty end of the bar.
A patron at the next booth slumps face-down into his plate. The Twi'lek across from him pockets something small from the table and stands. She makes eye contact with the players as she walks past.
A blaster bolt strikes the wall above the players' booth. Down the bar, two patrons have stood up; one of them has his weapon out and is aiming, not at the players, at the next booth over.
A panicked young human in a freighter crew jacket bursts through the door, scans the room, points directly at the players, and says, 'It's them. That's them.' Then he runs back out.

The serving droid stops mid-roll and recites, in the players' direction: 'Imperial customs inspection team has entered the docking bay where the customer's ship is parked. Continued message: They are opening the cargo hold.'
The Trandoshan from the corner has crossed to the players' booth. He sets a credit chit on the table and says, 'For the trouble. I need you out of the bar in two minutes. Pick a door.'
Two bounty hunters in matching short coats are working the room booth by booth, asking everyone the same question and checking a holo. They are three booths from the players.
Power cuts to the bar. Emergency strip lights snap on, red and low. In the dim, the back door swings open and three figures come through it fast and quiet.
The bartender ducks below the counter and comes back up with a stubby slug-thrower on the bar. She doesn't aim it. She looks at the front door. So does everyone else.

Behind the bar, a wall-mounted comm crackles with port chatter on low volume — incoming, outgoing, ground crew. A pilot at the counter listens without seeming to. The bartender stirs a pot of stew on a hot plate at the end of the back shelf.
A holo display behind the bar shows hyperlane congestion — long bars of red and orange. A spacer at the counter watches it with a thumb on her lip. The bartender pours her refill without being asked.
A pair of Imperial naval ratings have set up at the front table — boots up, helmets off, drinks halfway. Every spacer in the room is now sitting one stool further from the door.
The walls vibrate with the hum of the port's main generators next door. Drinks shiver in their cups. A patron at the bar steadies her glass with two fingers, mid-conversation, without missing a word.
Conversations drop to whispers when the door slides open. They resume when the patron entering is recognized. The bartender doesn't look up; she pulls a fresh mug down from the rack.
A serving girl, maybe sixteen, threading between tables with a tray. Calls every patron 'Captain.' Calls actual captains 'Sir' or 'Ma'am.' Has not yet been wrong.
A wiry Sullustan in port maintenance overalls. Polishes the same spot on the bar where he's drinking, idly, the entire time he's there. The spot is the cleanest in the room.
A Trandoshan at the back table, jaw scarred from old fights. Orders a drink, lets it sit, leaves, comes back twenty minutes later and orders the same drink again, lets it sit, leaves.
A young Zabrak in a freighter crew jacket. Asks every new patron at the bar where they're shipping out to, friendly, then writes the answer on her wrist with a stylus.
A heavyset human bouncer at the door, arms folded. Greets each entering patron by name. When he doesn't know one, he pretends to, and looks at the bartender until she nods.
A Pantoran navigator at a side table, scrolling through what looks like a starchart on a battered datapad. Mutters route names under his breath. When anyone passes, he flips the datapad to a recipe.
An old Aqualish dockmaster, missing one tusk. Refers to the current year as 'thirty-two,' which it isn't, and corrects everyone else when they say a different number.
A young human in port medic's coveralls at a side table, kit at her feet, drinking water. Looks at everyone's hands as they pass — checking knuckles, scars, recent burns.
A grey-haired Quarren at the bar, suction marks faded on one tentacle. Sniffs every drink before taking a sip, even his own, even ones he's already been drinking from.
A scrawny human in patched coveralls, a port engineer's insignia faded on the shoulder. Reads every entering patron's boots before their faces, and frowns at one in three.
A Twi'lek freight runner with red ink along her lekku — fresh, not yet healed. Switches to formal Huttese whenever a new patron approaches her end of the bar, and goes quiet if they answer in it.
An older Ithorian in stevedore harness, slow-moving, slow-speaking. Greets every Wookiee, Trandoshan, or Whiphid in the bar by full clan name and gets it right every time.
A young Devaronian deckhand at the bar, horns barely budding. Tries to order spice openly the first time, is corrected by the bartender quietly, and orders ale the rest of the night without comment.
A blind Rodian at the corner stool, milky eyes, ear-cones intent. Names every patron who walks past by the sound of their boots, every time, and is never wrong.
An old Mirialan in a faded captain's coat is selling a starchart at the corner table — actual flimsi, hand-annotated, not a chip. The buyer is examining it with a jeweler's loupe.
A young human in port crew greys is loudly buying drinks for the room and announcing she just got her pilot's certificate. The bartender quietly cuts her credit limit on the next round.
A heavyset Weequay in a mining tabard is being refused service by the bartender, hand flat on the bar between them, no argument, just a slow shake of the head. He doesn't leave.
A scrawny human kid in a delivery satchel is going booth to booth with a small parcel, reading each booth number off a flimsi. He stops at the booth before the players' and turns around.
A Mandalorian in scarred beskar is at the end of the bar, helmet off on the wood beside her. She has not taken off her gauntlets. Her drink sits untouched.
An Aqualish in port crew coveralls is filling a sack with bottles directly from the bar's shelf, the bartender ticking each one off on a flimsi. He pays in heavy offworld coin.
A wiry Kel Dor pilot in a worn mask is sketching the layout of the bar onto a bar napkin, slowly, marking exits. He folds the napkin into his collar when the bartender refills his glass.
A Twi'lek freighter captain is paying for someone else's tab at the bar — not the players', but the booth next to them. The patrons at that booth are still in mid-meal and haven't noticed.
A heavyset Trandoshan is asking the bartender, in a low voice, if 'the Twi'lek with the red lekku ink' has been in tonight. The bartender wipes the bar and says she hasn't seen anyone like that.
An old human pilot is teaching a young Sullustan to play a deck-of-cards game at the bar. They've been at it an hour. The pilot keeps losing on purpose.
A scrawny Bothan in a port engineer's coveralls at the bar, oil on her cheek, working through a fried plate one bite at a time.
An old human merchant at a side table, gloves off, blowing on a steaming bowl of stew.
A Sullustan freighter mechanic on a stool by the door, drink in one hand, datapad in the other, scrolling shipping schedules.
A young human in a flight crew jacket asleep against the wall in the corner booth, drink barely touched.
A Bith musician on break at the corner stool, instrument case at her feet, eyes closed, quiet.
An older Twi'lek freight handler is paying a tab in offworld coin, the bartender weighing each coin in a small scale on the bar.
A scrawny Rodian is sharpening a small knife on a whetstone in his lap, idly, between sips.
A young Pantoran serving girl asks the players quietly if any of them are 'the one who comms ahead.' Then she immediately apologizes and says she has them mixed up with another booth.
A Sullustan at the next stool over leans in and says, low: 'The man at the back booth has been describing your ship to the bartender. He says he was sent to pick something up from it.'

An old Devaronian at the bar slides a folded piece of flimsi toward the players along the wood, doesn't look at them, and goes back to his drink. The flimsi has a single hyperlane coordinate written on it.

A wiry human in port crew coveralls drops into the seat across from the players uninvited and says, friendly, 'I think we crewed together once. The Vandar run. Remember?' None of the players were on a Vandar run.
The bartender refills the players' drinks and says, quietly, 'You should know — the bay you're parked in just got reassigned in the port log. Whoever does that doesn't usually warn anyone.'
Two heavyset humans in matching short jackets have just walked in, ordered nothing, and are standing inside the doorway scanning faces. The bouncer has not moved to greet them.
A holocaster behind the bar cuts from sports to an Imperial bulletin: a port-wide ship inspection has been ordered. The bartender turns the volume up. Several patrons stand and pay tabs fast.
A young Mirialan slides into the booth opposite the players and sets a small datachip on the table between them. She says, 'He paid me to give you this. I don't know what's on it.' Then she leaves.
An ISB officer in charcoal has just walked in, alone, no escort, and ordered a drink. He hasn't looked toward the players. Patrons around him have begun, slowly, to settle their tabs.
The Trandoshan at the back booth has stood up. He's coming over. He's carrying a vibroblade in his right hand, point-down, not raised, just visible.
A bounty hunter in scarred armor has set a holo-projector on the bar. A rotating image hovers above it. It's one of the players' faces. The bounty hunter has not turned around.
A door alarm somewhere in the back of the bar starts blaring. The bartender swears and disappears through a hatch. Two patrons near the back exit are already standing.

The serving girl reaches the players' booth, sets down their drinks, and whispers, 'The man at the bar in the brown coat has been describing all four of you to someone on his comm. He thinks I can't hear him.'
A Mandalorian helmet appears in the window outside. The Mandalorian doesn't enter. They're just standing in the open doorway of the building across the street, watching the bar's front.
The lights in the bar dim by half. Every privacy field at every booth flickers and dies. Someone at the back booth swears. The bartender is already moving for the breaker.

A faint chemical smell hangs in the back — somebody is brewing something illegal in a back room and venting through the kitchen. The bartender pours a fresh round without comment. A patron sneezes once and lets it go.
A long shelf above the bar holds a row of empty bottles, dated in marker — keepsakes from regulars who didn't come back. The bartender adds a fresh empty to the end. She doesn't look at the rest.
Sand drifts in through the slightly open front door and pools at the threshold. No one closes the door. The serving droid wheels through the sand and leaves twin tracks across the floor.

The kitchen door swings open and a wall of cooking smell hits the room — fryer oil, spice, charred meat. A serving girl backs out balancing four plates. The smell follows her halfway across the floor.
A holo screen behind the bar plays an old swoop race in muted color, picture flickering with every voltage drop. A patron at the counter follows the race intently, drink forgotten in her hand.
